Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:45: Likewise, among the things that bring about clinging is for a person to seclude himself part of the day when he contemplates the greatness of the Former of all things, as explained in the Gate of Fear and the Gate of Love, and say with his mouth the later chapters of Job, and say them with understanding, with composure, and with a raised voice, and likewise several verses from David the king's psalms, peace be upon him, that recount the wonders of the Lord and His greatness. And so Rabbeinu Tam wrote in Sefer HaYashar, that a person should make it a habit to read once a week the response beginning "and the Lord answered Job from the whirlwind" (Job 38:3), "gird up your loins now like a man." And Rabbeinu Yonah wrote that one should read every day the passage (Deuteronomy 10:12), "what does the Lord your God ask of you, but to fear," etc.; therefore it is good to read both of these.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:46: Likewise, when a person reads every day the verses of song [Pesukei DeZimra], and says them with intent and with a raised voice, he will draw clinging upon himself; and so let him persist every day in reading the Book of Psalms with intent and a raised voice in the synagogue — and how good it is if he also intends them by way of the secret, with some of the customary designations found in the Zohar.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:47: Now, just as song brings about clinging, so Torah too is called song and brings about clinging, as our sages, of blessed memory, explained, "and in the night His song is with me" (Psalms 42:9) — the song of Torah is only at night. Now, the whole reality of song, whether the song of Torah or other songs, is all to arouse the Shechinah, as they say (ibid. 30:13), "so that glory may sing to You and not be silent; O Lord my God, forever I will thank You" — and it cannot be explained that all David said in the psalms was "forever," for when would his Torah study have taken place? Rather, surely engaging in Torah too is part of the thanksgiving and praise, as he says (ibid. 119:7), "I will thank You with an upright heart, when I learn Your righteous judgments."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:48: Part of loving the King is to honor Him and sing before Him in the synagogue, as it is the custom to sing before a king of flesh and blood — and the praise of a king is his honor, in the manner of (Psalms 29:9), "and in His Temple, all say, glory," and it says, "ascribe to the Lord glory and strength, ascribe to the Lord the glory of His name" — and by what is His name glorified? Surely through praise, song, and thanksgiving.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:49: In the Zohar (parashat Noach 73a), Rabbi Elazar opened and said (Isaiah 25:1), "O Lord, You are my God; I will exalt You, I will thank Your Name, for You have done wondrous things, counsels from afar, faithfulness and truth" — how much people ought to contemplate the honor of the Holy One, blessed be He, and praise His glory, for whoever knows how to praise his Master properly, the Holy One, blessed be He, does his will; and not only that, but he increases blessings above and below. Therefore, whoever knows how to praise his Master and to unify His Name is beloved above and desired below, and the Holy One, blessed be He, is praised through him in His glory, and of him it is written (Isaiah 49:3), "and He said to me, you are My servant, Israel, in whom I am glorified." — end of quotation. And further in the Zohar (parashat Vayechi 250a), on the verse (Isaiah 10:30), "cry aloud with your voice," etc., they say, in these words: and therefore, whoever increases praises to the Holy One, blessed be He, increases peace above; therefore, "hearken, O Laish [alt. "listen to the tribute"]." — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:50: Since we do not know how to compose praises, it is good that we say the praises of David the king, peace be upon him. David the king, peace be upon him, requested that his psalms be recited in synagogues and study halls, as it is said (Psalms 61:5), "I will dwell in Your tent forever" — David said, Master of the universe, may it be Your will that a matter [of Torah] be said in my name in this world (Bechorot 31b). Further, they said in the Midrash (Midrash Tehillim, mizmor 1): Rabbi Yirmeyah said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan: it is written, "I will dwell in Your tent forever" — does it enter your mind that David requested a dwelling in two worlds? Rather, he said, may it be Your will that they read and mention me in synagogues and study halls, as though I were still alive. — end of quotation. Further, our sages, of blessed memory, said (ibid.) that David requested that people study and read them and receive reward for them like [studying the laws of] plagues and tents, as it is said (ibid. 19:15), "let the words of my mouth be acceptable [before You]."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:51: In any case, one who reads the Book of Psalms in the synagogue, or liturgical poems and the like, should not raise his voice if he does not have a pleasant voice; and so it is said in the Zohar (parashat Vayechi 249b), on the verse (Isaiah 10:30), "cry aloud with your voice, O daughter of Gallim; hearken, O Laish" — in these words: "cry aloud with your voice" — this verse is said of the Assembly of Israel, because she praises the Holy One, blessed be He, with a praising voice; therefore, "cry aloud with your voice." From here we learn that whoever wishes to praise the Holy One, blessed be He, with his voice needs a pleasant voice, so that it is agreeable to others who hear it; and if not, he should not raise his voice. Come and see, the Levites who come from this side, as it is written (Numbers 8:25), "and from the age of fifty years he shall retire from the service work," etc. — end of quotation, as pertains here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:52: Just as the songs of Torah bring about clinging to Him, blessed be He, so the songs that women [sing, i.e., of a licentious nature], which are words of lust and coarse speech, bring about the separation of the soul from the bundle of life, and at the very least they are idle words that have no substance at all. And how many people of low soul are drawn after these debased songs and lose their soul — of them the prophet said (Amos 5:23), "take away from Me the noise of your songs, and let Me not hear the melody of your lutes," and it further says (ibid. 6:5), "who pluck on the lute-strings, and like David have invented for themselves instruments of song."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:53: Our sages, of blessed memory, said (Berachot 31a): Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rashbi: it is forbidden for a person to fill his mouth with laughter in this world, as it is said (Psalms 126:2), "then our mouth shall be filled with laughter and our tongue with joyous song; then shall they say among the nations, the Lord has done great things for these [people]" — they said of Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish that he never filled his mouth with laughter in this world from the time he learned this teaching from the mouth of Rabbi Yochanan, his teacher.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:54: Rabbeinu Yitzchak Alfasi, peace be upon him, transcribed regarding this teaching in Berachot everything relevant to this matter found in the Gemara, and therefore we thought fit to quote his words, in these words: we learn in Gittin, first chapter — they sent to Mar Ukva, from where do we know that music is forbidden? He ruled and wrote to them (Hosea 9:1), "do not rejoice, O Israel, to exultation, like the peoples," [meaning] send us also (Isaiah 24:9), "they shall not drink wine with song," etc. If this alone were the source, I would have said this refers only to music with instruments, but vocal music would be permitted; therefore he taught us that this too is forbidden. Ravina found Mar bar Rav Ashi weaving a wreath for his daughter. He said to him, do you not hold by what is said (Ezekiel 21:31), "remove the turban and lift off the crown" — when the turban is on the High Priest's head, the crown may be on every person's head; when the turban was removed from the High Priest's head, the crown was removed from every person's head. He said to him, this applies specifically to men, but for women it does not.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:55: We learn at the end of Sotah: Rav said, an ear that hears music should be uprooted. Rava said, music in a house is ruin at the doorway, as it is said (Zephaniah 2:14), "a voice shall sing in the window, desolation shall be in the threshold." Rav Yosef said, men singing and women responding is licentiousness; women singing and men responding is like fire in tow [flax] — what practical difference does this make? To determine which is to be abolished before the other.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:56: Rabbi Yochanan said: whoever drinks wine to the accompaniment of four kinds of music brings five punishments upon the world, as it is said (Isaiah 5:11), "woe to those who rise early in the morning to pursue strong drink, who linger late into the night, inflamed by wine," "and the harp, and the lute, the tambourine and the flute, and wine, are in their feasts." What is written after it? (ibid. 5:13), "therefore My people go into exile for lack of knowledge; their honored men are famished, and their multitude is parched with thirst."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:57: A Gaon explained: the ruling that vocal music is forbidden refers to things like love songs of one person for another, or praises of a person's beauty, such as what the Ishmaelites call "ash'ar" [poetry]; but words of songs and praises and remembrance of the kindnesses of the Holy One, blessed be He — no person of Israel refrains from these, and it is the custom of all Israel to say them at weddings and feasts with melodious voice and joyful voice, and we have not seen anyone protest this.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:58: We learn in the chapter Chelek (Sanhedrin 101a): our rabbis taught, one who reads a verse from Song of Songs and treats it as a kind of song, and one who reads a verse at an inappropriate time, brings evil upon the world, because the Torah girds itself with sackcloth and stands before the Holy One, blessed be He, and says: Master of the universe, Your children have made me like a harp that scoffers play upon. The Holy One, blessed be He, said to her: My daughter, if so, what shall My children do at a time when they eat and drink and rejoice? She said before Him: Master of the universe, if they are masters of Scripture, let them occupy themselves with Scripture — with the Prophets and the Writings; and if they are masters of Mishnah, let them occupy themselves with Mishnah — with halachot and aggadot; and if they are masters of Gemara, let them occupy themselves with Gemara — with the laws of Passover on Passover, the laws of Shavuot on Shavuot, the laws of the Festival on the Festival. Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar testified in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Chananyah: one who reads a verse at its proper time brings good to the world, as it is said (Proverbs 15:23), "a word spoken in its proper time, how good it is." — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:59: In the Tosefta to Sanhedrin, chapter 12, we say: Rabbi Akiva says, one who trills his voice on Song of Songs at a house of feasting, treating it as a kind of song, has no portion in the World to Come.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:60: Now it is already known what Rabbeinu Bachya said in Chovot HaLevavot (Gate of Self-Reckoning, ch. 3), that this world and the World to Come are like two rival wives — when you please one, you anger the other. In our own matter, know that it is impossible for a person to be attached to the joy of his Creator so long as he is joyful in worldly joy, in eating and drinking, as the prophet said (Isaiah 22:13), "and behold, joy and gladness, slaying oxen and slaughtering sheep, eating meat and drinking wine — eat and drink, for tomorrow we die" — what is written after it? "And it was revealed in my ears by the Lord of hosts, surely this iniquity shall not be atoned for you until you die," etc. And Solomon the king, peace be upon him, said (Ecclesiastes 7:4), "the heart of the wise is in the house of mourning, but the heart of fools is in the house of mirth," and the prophet Jeremiah said (Jeremiah 15:17), "I did not sit in the assembly of merrymakers, nor did I exult" — and our sages, of blessed memory, said in the Pesikta (DeRav Kahana, piska 15): the Assembly of Israel said before the Holy One, blessed be He: Master of the universe, I did not enter the theaters and circuses of the gentiles and play with them; because of Your hand I sat alone. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:61: Therefore it is not fitting to rejoice in the joy of this world, all of which passes away, as our sages, of blessed memory, expounded in Vayikra Rabbah, at the beginning of parashat Acharei Mot, in these words, on the verse (Psalms 75:5), "I said to the boastful, do not boast, and to the wicked, do not lift up the horn" — the Holy One, blessed be He, said to the wicked: the righteous did not rejoice in My world, and you seek to rejoice? Rabbi Levi said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya: the heel of the first man outshone the sphere of the sun — how much more so his facial features! And do not be surprised — it is the way of the world that a person makes for himself one garment for himself and one for his household; for whom does he make the finer one — is it not for himself? So too the first man was created for the service of the Holy One, blessed be He, while the sphere of the sun was created for the service of creatures. Rabbi Levi said in the name of Rabbi Chama bar Chanina: the Holy One, blessed be He, bound thirteen bridal canopies for him in Gan Eden, as it is said (Ezekiel 28:13), "you were in Eden, the garden of God," etc. — and after all this praise, "for you are dust, and to dust you shall return."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:62: Abraham did not rejoice in the world, and you seek to rejoice? A son was born to him at a hundred years, and in the end the Holy One, blessed be He, said to him, take now your son and go a three-day journey, etc. Israel did not rejoice in My world — it does not say "Israel rejoiced in his Maker" but rather "let Israel rejoice" [future] — they are destined to rejoice in the deeds of the Holy One, blessed be He, in the time to come. So to speak, the Holy One, blessed be He, Himself did not rejoice in His world, as it is said, "the Lord shall rejoice in His works" — it does not say "He rejoiced" but "He shall rejoice" [future] — the Holy One, blessed be He, is destined to rejoice in the deeds of the righteous in the time to come. — end of quotation, as pertains here. We have skipped much of the passage not necessary for our purpose.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:63: It is written in the Book of Ethical Traits found among us in manuscript (Orchot Tzaddikim, Gate of Joy) that one should not excessively engage in laughter, because it diminishes fear [of Heaven], in these words: at the time of laughter one cannot direct any fear of the Lord his God, and all the more so if he laughs through outings or gambling, in which the fear of God is not upon him; therefore a person should discipline his son so that he not excessively laugh, and should not acquire for him a teacher or friend to laugh with, as it is said (Jeremiah 15:17), "I did not sit in the assembly of merrymakers," and it is written (Proverbs 14:23), "in all labor there is profit [but idle talk leads only to loss]." There is much evil in [excessive] joy and laughter, such as rejoicing at a fellow's misfortune when some evil mishap of this world befalls him, of which it is said (ibid. 24:17), "when your enemy falls, do not rejoice, and when he stumbles, let not your heart be glad."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:64: There is a joy worse than this, such as rejoicing when one's fellows stumble in the service of the Creator, blessed be He, or rejoicing at their lesser knowledge — every servant who serves his master faithfully must know what he will say before his master, and you should be distressed when you see people rebelling against their Master, and mourn over them — then he is a faithful servant; but when a servant sees people belittling and reviling his master and he rejoices, this is not a faithful servant. Behold, Scripture says (Psalms 147:11), "the Lord desires those who fear Him" — and whoever rejoices at his fellow's stumbling, his will is not in accord with the Creator's will. Regarding this Rabbi Nechunya ben HaKanah prayed (Berachot 28b): "may my colleagues not stumble in a matter of halachah, that I not rejoice over them; and may I not stumble, that they rejoice over me" — and Rabbi Nechunya prayed this because he saw that it was common for one to rejoice at a fellow's mishap so that he might triumph over his fellow and gain renown from it, and he even saw important people who were not careful about this. Therefore every person whose will is like God's will should be distressed that God's will is not done, and should even pray for his enemy that he serve the Creator, and should direct his heart in prayer, in the blessing "You who graciously grant [knowledge]," and in the blessing "return us, our Father," and "forgive us, our Father," for all of Israel, those who love him and those who hate him, and so in all the blessings — for how could it be that one prays for the healing of the sickness of the people Israel and yet does not wish his fellow to be healed? And so with the other blessings. And because this inclination is habitual in the hearts of all people, and one does not sense this matter, it was written to warn out of fear of the Lord, blessed be He, to prepare their hearts for God with complete and true intent, to pour out their soul before the Name for all of Israel, both those who love him and those who hate him — and thus "and you shall love your fellow as yourself" will be fulfilled, and "he who is clean of hands shall increase in strength."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:65: There is a joy and laughter worse than this — such as one who laughs at someone who is careful in the service of the Creator, blessed be He, and who fulfills His commandments — and there are four evils in this. The first, that he darkens his own soul from the light of the commandments — when he despises and laughs at those who fulfill the commandments, then the commandments become repugnant in his own eyes. The second, that perhaps, because of the laughter, the righteous person will be deterred from his righteousness, unable to bear the laughter. The third, that many people who have not been tested to walk in the ways of the Lord will be unable to repent because of the laughter, and will walk in darkness all their days; it follows that this scoffer is not content merely to withhold from his fellow the abundant good hidden away for the righteous, but brings him down to the lowest depths — and behold, this scoffer is included in the punishment of one who causes the multitude to sin. The fourth, that he resembles bandits who stand at the crossroads and cut off the feet of those bringing gifts to the king — are they not enemies of the king, and their wickedness very great?
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:66: There is a joy more bitter than wormwood — such as those who pursue adultery, robbery, and other transgressions, and rejoice in achieving their evil desires; of this it is said (Proverbs 2:14), "who rejoice in doing evil, who delight in the perversities of evil" — and their punishment is great, down to the lowest depths of Sheol.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:67: There is a joy mixed with smoke that rises over all the commandments, that makes the fear of the Lord, blessed be He, forgotten from the hearts of human beings — such as those who become drunk and rejoice in houses of feasting, and the end of joy is grief, for much corruption comes from the way of the laughter of feasting. And who is as wise as Solomon son of David, who said (ibid. 23:29), "who has woe? Who has sorrow? Who has strife? Who has complaint? Who has wounds without cause? Who has redness of eyes? Those who linger long over wine, those who go to seek out mixed wine." Also the prophet Isaiah said (Isaiah 5:12), "but they do not regard the work of the Lord, nor see the deeds of His hands," and it is written (Proverbs 20:1), "wine is a mocker, strong drink is raging, and whoever is deceived by it is not wise."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:68: Having explained the nature of joy and its opposite, we thought fit to explain in several ways in what we are obligated regarding it. We say: since it is true that love and joy are both one matter, as explained, whoever wishes to be a chasid and be called a lover [oheiv] of the seed of Abraham, of whom it is said (Isaiah 41:8), "the seed of Abraham, My beloved," must be joyful when blessing the Holy One, blessed be He, in the blessing of enjoyment, and likewise in his prayer, his Torah, and his commandments, and in receiving people with joy, and on the days of the festivals, as we explained above.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:69: In his blessings he should intend to give praise and thanks to the Cause of All who created that thing, and through the praise he clings to the love of the Creator, His greatness and His exaltedness. We have already said that all the supernal beings and souls above, all of them praise the Creator for the good they receive from Him, and the Cause of All never withholds His flow and light from bestowing — and for this we are obligated to bless Him. For this reason are the blessings that the Men of the Great Assembly instituted over every single thing, so that we remember the Holy One, blessed be He's, love, His greatness, His exaltedness, and His constant providence over us at all times — that He created that thing through His flow, by the power of His supernal attributes, so that those below might benefit from His flow, and through it we cling to Him forever. Therefore one must give praise and blessing to the Creator with a good heart, a good eye, and with joy; and so it is explained in the Zohar (beginning of parashat Bamidbar), on the verse (Psalms 115:12), "the Lord has remembered us, He will bless" — that when a person mentions his fellow's praise, he must bless him so that the evil eye not rule over him, and it says: whoever blesses his fellow, the Holy One, blessed be He, wishes to bless him with a good eye and a good heart; whoever blesses the Holy One, blessed be He, all the more so requires a good eye, a good heart, and love of the heart — therefore, "and you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart." — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:70: Now, from worldly matters a person may take a lesson for the love of the Holy One, blessed be He. It is known that one who gives a gift to his fellow without any prior favor owed by his fellow, the recipient of that gift is obligated to love the giver, even if the gift is small. Now the Holy One, blessed be He, who gives everything and gives to all, as it is said (I Chronicles 29:14), "for everything is from You" — without doubt, love toward Him, blessed be He, is obligatory upon man. And when a person contemplates this while reciting the blessing of enjoyment, love will be aroused in his heart. However, one who blesses without intending to give praise to the Creator, blessed be He, is punished, as they said in Sefer Chasidim; see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:71: Further, one who blesses with joy and a good heart becomes a chariot for the attribute of Chesed — for just as the attribute of Chesed bestows with generosity, without hesitation, willingly and joyfully, since joy stems from its side as explained, so is one who blesses, in the manner of (Genesis 12:3), "and I will bless those who bless you" — for just as he desires to bestow blessings on the Assembly of Israel out of Chesed, so blessings are bestowed upon him out of Chesed, and this is called "a good eye."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:72: Just as a person is obligated to be joyful on days of joy, so must he mourn on days of distress — such as the four fasts, "the fast of the fourth [month]," etc. (Zechariah 8:19), and the twenty-one days between the seventeenth of Tammuz and the ninth of Av, all of which are days of distress and sorrow. Likewise, on days that are not days of joy, it is good to mourn every day over the destruction of the Temple and over His profaned Name among the nations, as it says in Tanna Devei Eliyahu, quoted in the Yalkut (parashat Ki Tissa, siman 391) — that one must sigh over the honor of the Omnipresent and the honor of Israel all his days, and desire, long for, and await the honor of Jerusalem and the honor of Israel and the honor of the Temple and the salvation that will soon sprout forth. — end of quotation, as pertains here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:73: In the Zohar (parashat Shemot, end of p. 17), they explained, of blessed memory: Rabbi Yehudah came to Rabbi Elazar and found him sitting with his hand on his mouth, sorrowful. He said to him, what is my master occupied with? He said to him: it is written (Proverbs 16:15), "in the light of the King's face is life." From this we may understand the obligation of humility and sorrow — for if you lift your eyes to heaven you will see the diminishment of the flow, for all faces have gathered pallor from what it was in the miracles and wonders of the days of old and the years of ancient times; and therefore it is fitting to banish natural joy and turn our spirits to Him, making it a basis, this being the contentment the Omnipresent has from us, so that He may bestow upon our souls His goodness upon us in the secret of creation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:74: He further says in Pesikta Rabbati (parashah 26), on "she who bore seven has languished" (Jeremiah 15:9): Jeremiah said, when I was going up to Jerusalem, I lifted my eyes and saw a certain woman sitting at the top of the mountain, clothed in black, her hair disheveled, crying out and asking, who will comfort her, and I too was crying out and asking, who will comfort me? I drew near to her and spoke with her: if you are a woman, speak with me; and if you are a spirit, depart from before me. She answered and said to me: do you not recognize me? I am she who had seven sons; their father went out to a country across the sea, and while I was still going up and weeping for him, a second [messenger] came and told me, the house has fallen on your seven sons and killed them — I do not know for whom to weep or for whom to loosen my hair. I said to her: are you better than Mother Zion, who has become a pasture for the beasts of the field? She answered and said to me: I am your Mother Zion, who has become a pasture for the beasts of the field; I am she who bore seven, for so it is written, "she who bore seven has languished." Jeremiah said to her: your wound is like the wound of an enemy — "shake yourself from the dust, arise, sit, O Jerusalem." — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:75: In the Midrash Eichah, from the Zohar, they elaborated at length on the matter of weeping over the exile and the destruction; see there. And whoever mourns over Jerusalem merits to see her comfort, as it is said (Isaiah 66:10), "rejoice with her in joy, all you who mourn over her" (Ta'anit 30b).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:1: Having explained in the preceding chapters the nature of love and the things that give birth to love, as found in the words of the Rashbi, peace be upon him, and in the words of our sages, of blessed memory, we wish to explain the preparations a person must engage in with his own body to acquire love, so that it be firmly fixed in his heart like a peg that shall not slip.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:2: These preparations Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair, peace be upon him, explained (Avodah Zarah 20b), in these words: our rabbis taught: "and you shall guard yourself from every evil thing" (Deuteronomy 23:10) — that a person should not have improper thoughts by day and come thereby to impurity at night. From here Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair said: Torah leads to watchfulness [zehirut], watchfulness leads to alacrity [zerizut], alacrity leads to cleanliness [nekiyut], cleanliness leads to abstinence [perishut], abstinence leads to purity [taharah], purity leads to holiness [kedushah], holiness leads to humility [anavah], humility leads to fear of sin [yir'at chet], fear of sin leads to piety [chasidut], piety leads to the holy spirit [ruach hakodesh], the holy spirit leads to the resurrection of the dead — and piety is greater than all of these, as it is said (Psalms 89:20), "then You spoke in a vision to Your pious ones." And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi disagrees, for Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said, humility is greater than all of these, as it is said (Isaiah 61:1), "the spirit of the Lord God is upon me, because the Lord has anointed me to bring good tidings to the humble" — it does not say "to the pious" but "to the humble" — from this you learn that humility is greater than all of these. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:3: Now, according to Rabbi Pinchas's view, that piety is greater than all of these, this is what we intended to explain in this passage for the exposition of love. The reason is that the Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Zohar that piety and love are one and the same matter, and with these was Rabbi Pinchas, peace be upon him, crowned — the proof of this being what is said in the Zohar, Bereishit (end of p. 11), regarding the second commandment, which is love: Rabbi Elazar said, Father, I have heard a beloved teaching about this; he said to him, my son, say it before Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair, for he stands at this very rank. And in parashat Acharei Mot (p. 62), Rabbi Shimon, peace be upon him, praised Rabbi Pinchas for the attribute of piety, and expounded to praise him with the verse (Psalms 149:5), "let the pious exult in glory," in these words: and behold, Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair is the crown of Chesed, the supernal head; therefore, "the pious shall inherit glory from above." — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:4: It is a simple matter that love and kindness [chesed] are all one, as it is said (Jeremiah 31:2), "with an everlasting love have I loved you, therefore with kindness have I drawn you," and likewise (Psalms 31:24), "love the Lord, all His pious ones." Therefore we thought fit to explain this passage, which explains the grades that lead to piety, which is love; and when a person fulfills these grades, love, which is piety, will be firmly fixed in his heart, and he will be bound to his God always, in such a manner that he will merit the holy spirit.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:5: Rashi, peace be upon him, explained this baraita, in these words: "and you shall guard yourself from every evil thing" (Deuteronomy 23:10), and immediately after it, "if there be among you a man who is not clean, by reason of that which happens to him by night" — and it warns him to guard himself so as not to come to this. "Torah" — through his engaging in it, and also that he sees and understands the warnings within it and is thereby guarded. "Zerizut" — being guarded beforehand so that sin does not come into his hand, this being when he does not have improper thoughts leading to impurity. "Zehirut" — when a sin comes into his hand, he is careful to guard himself from stumbling in it — and so we say regarding "all flesh" (Chullin 107b): does this not mean he was careful and did not touch it? No — it means he was quick and washed his hands beforehand. "Nekiyut" [cleanliness] — clean of any sin. "Perishut" [abstinence] — he abstains even from what is permitted, to be strict with himself. "Tahor" [pure] — bright and refined, superior even to "clean." "Leading to the holy spirit" — to cause the Shechinah to rest upon him. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:6: Rabbeinu Nissim quoted the words of Rashi, peace be upon him, and added an explanation of humility, fear of sin, and piety, in these words: through this he comes to humility, because he despises the affairs of this world; and from this he comes to fear of sin, for he fears it as one fears an enemy; and from this he comes to piety — that all his deeds are for the sake of Heaven. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:7: Now we wish to expand the explanation of the words of Rashi, of blessed memory, peace be upon him, and to explain each and every word mentioned in this passage according to its usage in Torah, Prophets, and Writings.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:8: "Torah leads to alacrity" — this matter is explained in several places, that study leads to action, and they said in Torat Kohanim (beginning of parashat Bechukotai): "if you walk in My statutes" — that you labor in Torah; "and you shall observe and do them" — one who learns in order to do; "but if you do not listen and do not do" — whoever does not learn does not do; in the end he despises others, in the end he despises the sages, in the end he does not let others perform [the commandments], in the end he does not acknowledge the commandments given to Moses at Sinai, in the end he denies the fundamental principle [of faith]. — end of quotation. Here it is explained that one who engages in Torah is thereby necessarily brought to action, as Rashi, of blessed memory, explained, that through seeing the warnings and punishments written in it, one is guarded from sin.
